unit.title: Seva, the Golden Temple, and Gratitude

lesson.title: The Real Jobs That Make Langar Work
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned Seva means helping without expecting anything back. Today: the real, specific jobs that make Langar actually happen!

Langar takes many different Seva jobs working together: some people cook the food, some serve it to everyone sitting together, some wash the dishes afterward, and some welcome guests as they arrive. Every single job matters equally — washing dishes is just as important as cooking, because Langar can't work without every part. If you visited a Gurdwara's Langar, which job would you most want to help with, and why?

You now understand that Langar isn't just one act of kindness — it's many different jobs, all equally important, working together. Tomorrow we'll learn a real detail about the Golden Temple you may not know yet.

objectives: Name at least three specific jobs that make Langar happen: cooking, serving, washing dishes
Explain why every Langar job matters equally, not just the more visible ones
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review Seva and Langar from last week.
2. Introduce the specific jobs: cooking, serving, dishwashing, welcoming.
3. Discuss why every job matters equally.
4. Have the child choose which job they'd want to help with, and why.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Close by connecting this to a real or hypothetical Langar visit.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two jobs (cooking and serving) before adding the less-visible ones
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one more job Langar might need that wasn't mentioned
This lesson deepens last week's Langar introduction with real specificity, rather than repeating the same general definition
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a discussion and drawing activity — check that the child can name at least three real Langar jobs and explain why they all matter equally.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'Seva (selfless service) and kindness' description, deepening last week's Langar introduction with concrete, specific detail.
